Subject: Grounding evaluation recap + reranker tradeoffs — Lumera Health

Hi Samantha / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the follow-ups we promised: we ran a short baseline sweep this morning against the sample clinical KB you shared (appointments_faqs + drug_guidance) and pulled together an initial set of numbers and recommendations. High-level takeaways below; full artifacts attached and linked.

TL;DR
- Best fit for Lumera’s latency/accuracy targets: Falcon-40B-8k quantized (int8) with a learned-similarity reranker on top (ensembles showed diminishing returns).
- If you need lower token cost and can accept slightly looser grounding, try Mistral-7B-16k + aggressive prefix caching + tuned retrieval (higher recall window).

Benchmarks we ran (attached: lumera_benchmark_v1.csv):
- Generation R-Precision @5 (retriever only): 68%
- Post-reranker top-1 grounding rate: 83% (Falcon-40B int8 + LR-reranker)
- Latency (p95) with continuous batching: 180ms/token for Falcon-40B (on dedicated A100 pool), 95ms/token for Mistral-7B
- Cost per 1k tokens (approx): $0.95 (Falcon-40B int8), $0.28 (Mistral-7B)

Reranker notes (summary in reranker_eval_summary.pdf):
- Learned-sim (BCE fine-tune on your relevance labels) produced the best top-1 precision with reasonable latency impact (+25ms).
- Cross-encoder approaches improved precision by ~5 points but doubled CPU cost in our setup — good for nightly batch reranks, not for strict 200ms p95 SLOs.
- Sparse lexical boosting (BM25 + keyword anchors) helped on short clinical phrases where the dense retriever missed edge-cases.

Suggested retrieval settings for pilot run:
- Retriever: dense encoder (bi-encoder) with index refresh cadence: 6h for your KB (documents are fairly static).
- Top-k retrieval to send to reranker: 20 (we saw best tradeoff at k=15-25).
- Reranker budget: keep to top-1 live, compute top-3 offline for diagnostics.
- KV cache: enable document-prefetch for repeat queries (reduced tokens by ~8% in session flows).

Next steps / asks from Lumera:
1) Confirm whether you prefer the Falcon-40B int8 path (higher accuracy, higher cost) or the Mistral-7B path (lower cost, lower latency).
2) Share a slightly larger sample of user prompts (50–100 edge-case queries) and any additional labels for grounding correctness — we’ll integrate into the reranker fine-tune. (prompt_suite_v2.txt attached as a starter)
3) Approval for a 2-week pilot on Dedicated (we’ll provision a small reserved pool) — Camila can share pricing/contract.

I’m copying Camila for contracting and Ben for the reranker fine-tune plan.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

1) Our clinical compliance team is sensitive to hallucinations around drug interactions — top priority is correctness over conversational polish. That pushes us toward the Falcon path if it materially reduces hallucination rate.
2) For the pilot scope, we can provide ~75 edge-case prompts and a small set of annotated ground-truth answers. We’ll send by EOD Monday.
3) On latency: 200ms p95 is our hard requirement for patient-facing chat flows. If Falcon-40B p95 is 180ms/token, can you confirm end-to-end for a 75-token average output?

One more ask: can you include an explicit test in the eval for “medical-assertion hallucination” (we’ll provide a checklist) and report precision/recall for those cases?

Hi all —

Quick answers to Samantha’s points and a short technical note on the hallucination test: 

- End-to-end latency: 180ms/token is model-response generation only (server-side). For a 75-token average output, expect ~13.5s if naive multiply — but that’s misleading because the runtime pipelines token generation and network hops differently. With continuous batching disabled for patient-facing real-time flow and with warm KV cache, our measured median end-to-end for 75-token responses on dedicated A100 was ~1.6s and p95 ~2.3s in our bench (includes retrieval + reranker + generation). Those numbers assume the reranker runs at +25ms and retrieval is sub-120ms. We’ll reproduce a 75-token end-to-end run in the pilot baseline.

- Medical-assertion hallucination test: Ben here will design a checklist and an eval probe. Proposed metrics: hallucination_rate (binary labels), incorrect_factual_claims (normalized), and safety_false_negative (cases where model omits mandatory warnings). We’ll add these to the dashboard and flag regressions relative to your annotated set.

- Reranker tradeoff suggestion: start with a dense bi-encoder retriever + light cross-encoder reranker (learned-sim for production top-1, nightly cross-encoder re-rank for diagnostics). This hybrid minimizes live CPU while giving you nightly high-accuracy views for audit.

Action items I’ll take on: produce the hallucination probe, add the 75-token end-to-end benchmark, and run a Mistral vs Falcon head-to-head with the provided prompts once we have your annotated set.

Ben Carter
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
